unit.definition: an already-closed ConferenceOS issue, replayed against the commit its fix landed on top of
unit.base_commit_rule: first parent of the merge commit of the PR that closed the issue
unit.checkout_rule: fresh mktemp -d scratch dir; git init + fetch --depth 1 --no-tags at base_commit; remote removed; NEVER reused
unit.leakage_rule: fail-closed under set -euo pipefail: total object census — the scratch store's full object list (cat-file --batch-all-objects) must exactly equal the base commit's reachable closure (rev-list --objects HEAD), compared via files with non-emptiness guards; plus rev-list --count --all == 1 and an empty `git remote` listing; blind brief (no canonical path/issue URL/PR number); post-run transcript audit for canonical path, github.com, gh/git-fetch, issue or PR numbers — any failed assertion or audit hit voids the run
unit.no_push: raw-arm output is never pushed anywhere; deliverable is an exported patch
unit.dependency_provisioning: coordinator runs `npm ci && npx prisma generate` in the scratch tree BEFORE dispatch, with network; install time/tokens excluded from metrics 3-4 in both arms; node_modules is git-ignored and derives only from the base commit's lockfile
unit.network_isolation: SUPERSEDED framing — see isolation_profile. Network denial alone was rejected: measured on host 2026-08-21, `codex -s workspace-write` blocks network but leaves the canonical checkout readable (RC=0), while `grok --sandbox strict` blocks the checkout but not network (HTTP:200). Neither CLI closes both vectors on macOS.
unit.implementer_platform: grok, both arms — forced by the macOS sandbox matrix above; holds platform constant across arms and removes a confound
unit.judge: Devin only. Grok implemented both arms; Claude never judges; Codex has seen harness-arm output as reviewer. If Devin is unavailable, judging blocks rather than falling back.
unit.harness_reviewer: Codex (not Grok, which implements), under the same isolation profile
unit.brief_sanitization: issue title+body with every #NNNN replaced by an opaque token ([REF-A], [REF-B], ...), every owner/repo slug and URL removed; sanitized text stored at paper/experiment/briefs/<code-name>.txt and given verbatim to the blind judge as the task statement
unit.void_run_rule: a run failing any leakage layer leaves status at 'ready' and appends to that task's void_runs array; void runs are reported as attempts-per-completed-task, never silently dropped
unit.isolation_profile: BOTH arms (owner decision 2026-08-21): project-scoped grok sandbox profile `ab219` written into the disposable scratch tree — extends=strict, read_only grants the node toolchain (required; strict alone hides $HOME/.hermes and makes the done-gate unrunnable), deny=[/Users/mrhinkle/Code, ~/.config/gh, ~/.ssh, ~/Documents]. Dispatched with GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN scrubbed and --disable-web-search. VERIFIED on host: node v22.22.3 usable; canonical checkout -> Operation not permitted (kernel); curl -> HTTP:200 (network NOT denied).
unit.vector_a_network: mitigated by credential denial, NOT network denial: repo is private (unauth GET of fixing PR -> 404, probed), tokens scrubbed, ~/.config/gh kernel-denied, web_search/web_fetch disabled. Residual general web access is DETECTION-ONLY via the retained transcript audit.
unit.vector_b_local_filesystem: closed at the kernel by the deny list — the canonical checkout and sibling worktrees carry the full future history including the fix and need no credentials; this is the higher-value vector
unit.containerized_runner: recommended hardening if the vector-A residual is unacceptable: container/VM with the scratch tree as the only mount and egress limited to the inference endpoint. Docker present (20.10.24) but daemon not running. NOT silently substituted for what was asked.
